items.title: Google DevSite爆RCE漏洞，偽造Cookie即可觸發
items.summary: Google開發者網站共用平臺DevSite被發現存在遠端程式碼執行（RCE）漏洞，問題出在Google將OAuth用戶端密鑰存放在瀏覽器Cookie內，又使用同一把密鑰作為Cookie簽章金鑰。資安研究人員Simon Koeck揭露，攻擊者無須登入Google帳號，就能利用這項漏洞在伺服器上執行任意程式碼。

items.title: OpenSSF與OpenChain提軟體供應鏈安全指引，協助企業因應CRA等歐盟法規
items.summary: 歐盟近年透過《網路韌性法》（CRA）及NIS2指令，分別提高數位產品及組織供應鏈的資安管理要求。開放原始碼安全基金會（OpenSSF）與OpenChain專案共同提出軟體供應鏈安全指引，建議企業建立內部管理流程，並在軟體開發及維護過程中落實安全措施，包括管理軟體元件、處理漏洞及保存安全佐證資料，以回應客戶審查及相關法規要求。

items.title: Upwind併購AI資安新創Aegis，成立研究團隊擴大AI代理安全布局
items.summary: 雲端資安業者Upwind宣布併購以色列AI資安新創Aegis，並成立AI安全研究團隊Upwind AI Lab，結合Aegis的研究團隊與技術，以及Upwind既有的雲端安全能力，擴大AI安全研發布局。新團隊將投入AI系統防護、利用AI代理協助資安維運、頂尖AI模型評測及進階AI系統研究。

items.title: PQC轉型不只升級系統，澳洲ASD強調教育訓練與長期維護
items.summary: 企業因應未來量子電腦對傳統密碼學的威脅，除了需要升級既有系統、導入抗量子密碼演算法，也必須讓相關人員具備部署及維護新密碼學機制所需的知識。澳洲政府情報與資安機構澳洲通訊局（ASD）公布後量子密碼學（Post-Quantum Cryptography，PQC）轉型系列的第五階段建議，將重點放在跨部門溝通、教育訓練及長期維護，強調企業不能將PQC轉型視為一次性的系統升級工作。

items.title: Python 3.15預設用UTF-8編碼，並新增延遲匯入機制
items.summary: Python開發團隊發布Python 3.15，預設採用UTF-8文字編碼，減少程式在不同作業系統讀寫文字時的差異，並新增延遲匯入機制，讓指定模組等到實際使用時才載入，以縮短程式啟動時間。新版也改進實驗性編譯器及自由執行緒版本的擴充模組支援。 過去Python程式讀寫文字檔時，如果沒有指定編碼，可能依作業系統及語言設定採用不同方式，導致同一份檔案在不同臺電腦可能出現亂碼或讀取錯誤。Python 3.15改以UTF-8處理未指定編碼的文字資料，已明確設定編碼的程式則不受影響。

items.summary: fix(media): keep Windows-1252 accents in channel attachments declared as text (#165771) fix(media): keep Windows-1252 inference for text/plain and text/csv attachments Attachments declared as text/plain or text/csv without a charset skipped the existing Windows-1252 inference, so accents and euro signs became replacement characters in model input; input_file also dropped an explicit charset before classification. Inference now applies whenever no charset is declared, and an explicit charset still wins. Proof: built Gateways, real /v1/responses input_file requests to a scripted provider: main model input `Caf� �`, candidate `Café €` for text/plain and text/csv. UTF-8 and explicit utf-8/windows-1252 controls unchanged. Thanks @yetval. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: refactor(extensions): simplify plugin paths and lifecycle bookkeeping…
items.summary: refactor(extensions): simplify plugin paths and lifecycle bookkeeping (#170511) ## What Problem This Solves Consolidate duplicate extension paths and remove speculative lifecycle defenses in Codex, Memory Core, Microsoft Teams, Matrix, Reef, and Workboard. The candidate removes **522 net production lines** (tests, fixtures, generated files, declaration files, and documentation excluded; both new production modules included). This uses the campaign's honest 500–999-line fallback after the scoped growth/largest-first pass; it does not remove features to reach a quota. Workboard's four card actions now share one discriminated action component, its draft controls share one renderer, and menu-only pass-through components are gone. Reef's worker and released-host adapters share one pure seven-command trust-transition policy while retaining their own atomic storage boundaries. Teams reuses its Graph/context/setup owners. Memory keeps normal parallel-query and sync-generation retirement draining, expressed with simpler active-completion tracking rather than nested borrower wrappers. An adjacent Workboard defect is fixed: conditional Solid fragments could run a popover ref before the preceding trigger entered the document, positioning the details menu at the page origin. Listener/anchor setup now runs after the DOM commit. The regression fails against the unchanged implementation and passes with this repair. No SDK export, config, protocol, dependency, database schema, durability, retention, or permission contract is changed. The protected standalone session-memory backend is untouched. No changelog edit. User impact: Workboard details menus anchor to their trigger instead of the page origin. Other changes simplify internal implementation, with the best-effort timing and diagnostic compromises below; no migration or operator action is required. ## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted - Codex diagnostic accessors throwing or mutable transport identities: [#163388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163388) adds synthetic throwing-accessor coverage, not an actual-use human report. Actual accessors are local reads and registration publishes frozen identities. Accessor programmer errors now surface; the diagnostic sink catch, disclosure allowlist, attempt isolation, and timeout/cleanup behavior remain. - Offline Codex migration CAS conflicts: [#168479](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168479) introduced retry loops without a human competing-writer report. Gateway ownership excludes live foreign writers. One atomic attempt plus existing persisted-result validation now retains the source sidecar and reports a warning on conflict; a later Doctor run can retry. - Retired Codex legacy JSON rewritten during migration: [#104504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104504) added a synthetic locator-rewrite test; human [#104503](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/104503) concerns fingerprint overflow, whose fix remains. Legacy indexes are offline inputs, so a second locator/lifecycle read is removed. Initial containment/malformed-owner validation and canonical session ownership checks remain; unsupported concurrent legacy edits are picked up next run. - Memory manager acquisition repeatedly retrying failed global retirement: [#144252](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144252) has synthetic close failures, no human incident requiring recursive acquisition recovery. Acquisition now awaits the pending close once and reports its error; the retirement owner is retained and explicit close can retry. - Abandoned, abort-ignoring memory diagnostic probes holding provider retirement indefinitely: [#113471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113471) and [#166973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166973) provide synthetic lifecycle proof, not a human abandoned-probe incident. Timed-out read-only diagnostics no longer retain a redundant inner borrower. Ordinary active searches, sync generations, healthy operations, and custom closable-provider draining remain protected. - Teams simultaneous Gateway writers: [#88411](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88411) introduced the persistence migration/file lock without a human multi-Gateway incident and did not test live tenant traffic. The Gateway is the sole database owner. Removed cross-process stale-lock/backoff machinery; local FIFO remains. Unsupported simultaneous processes may overwrite each other rather than coordinate. - Workboard stale cache publication and an exact-expiry late join: [#165896](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165896), [#165141](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165141), and [#165698](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165698) use synthetic performance/interleaving controls, not a human incident. One read may return an older projection/fallback; normal revision/age invalidation refreshes it next read. Measured caching, the 64-entry bound, and read authority remain. - Workboard direct stop/start before asynchronous startup settles: [#146976](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146976) forces unsupported lifecycle ordering in a test. The host service owner already awaits raw startup before stop. Removed plugin-local generation/startup handoff; supported host lifecycle is unchanged, unsupported direct reentry no longer has a second lifecycle owner. - Reef failed owner-notice dispatch/ack retry timing: [#109160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109160) pins injected failures and exponential timers, without a human report requiring that second scheduler. Durable pending notices now retry during ordinary successful 30-second reconciliation or restart. A failed acknowledgement may redispatch conservative stop-only guidance; durable resend reservation/cooldown prevents granting a second resend. The per-peer queue also makes the removed in-flight set redundant. - Reef synchronous intermediate lease theft: [#109380](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109380) and [#168340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168340) describe synthetic interleavings, not human concurrent-writer incidents. SDK callbacks commit synchronously and there is no await between acquisition and settlement. Unsupported reentrant callbacks/foreign writers are no longer checked at every intermediate step. Initial acquisition, final head-owner check, staged recovery, uncertain-commit witness, rollback, and retention ordering remain. - Workboard fabricated native event targets and repeated widget predicates: renderer port [#168606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168606) added boilerplate without a human incident. JSX native bindings already guarantee `currentTarget` types, and the owning menu already excludes widgets. Fabricated direct handler calls may throw; real event dispatch, widget behavior, and untrusted `event.target` checks are unchanged. ## Coverage ledger Discovery began with scoped three-day growth, then fourteen-day history and largest production owners. Each removed mechanism was checked against its introduction and current callers; no dormant/in-flight foundation was deleted. Exact and normalized duplicate scans informed structural inspection, not automatic rewrites. | Owner / original location | Decision and evidence | | --- | --- | | Codex `app-server/request-diagnostics.ts:28,109,133` | Remove speculative accessor catches/identity copy; keep timeout sink and disclosure boundary (#163388). | | Codex `command-handler-actions.ts:109` | Share sandbox/execution result assembly; preserve policy selectors, guards, currentness and release. | | Codex `migration/session-binding-sidecars.ts:460,549,627` | Single CAS attempt and one legacy-input read; preserve sidecar on conflict and canonical effect validation (#168479, #104504). | | Codex `installed-probe.ts:29`, native session preparation/monitor | KEEP isolated managed storage, credentials, native execution authority and ordinary write settlement. Upstream configuration/storage contract inspected directly. | | Memory `memory/search-deadline.ts:42` | One rejected cancellation promise replaces sentinel race; preserve cancellation/error identity, abort ordering, wall-clock guard and cleanup (#95757, #147702). | | Memory `manager-embedding-ops.ts:84`, `manager-registry.ts:264` | Simplify nested borrower bookkeeping and failed-close recovery; preserve outer leases, normal drain and documented retiring-cache fence (#113471, #166973, #144252). An initially broader removal was rejected during review. | | Memory publication, database context, index generation, transfer and cache owners | KEEP user-data transaction/publication, Forget exclusion, bounded transfers, worker ownership, integrity, performance caches and normal shutdown settlement (#168860, #169164, #169251, #170183, #170302, #170407). | | Memory paused deadlines, Unicode query, KNN/vector scan, watchers | KEEP human-reported SQLite stalls (#137056), dependency tokenizer behavior, external/native input validation, bounded resources and realistic cancellation. | | Memory dreaming/REM, migration/repair, backfill and standing intents | KEEP user-facing features, privacy/source validation, persisted rollback and public formats. Phase E untouched. | | Teams `sqlite-state.ts:27`, `graph.ts:85,177` | Remove redundant foreign-writer lock; one guarded Graph transport retains auth/SSRF, bounded parsing and release (#88411). | | Teams `setup-surface.ts:102`, `graph-group-management.ts:32,96`, `channel.ts:267` | Consolidate identical saves/context/pending result bookkeeping; preserve provider-specific validation, labels, errors, ordering and direct results (#112811). | | Matrix `matrix/actions/reactions.ts:135` | Remove duplicate missing-sender/empty-result guards; selector remains ownership boundary, empty list has no redactions. | | Matrix crypto store, verification, readiness, send FIFO and thread binding owners | KEEP room-key durability, real throwing dependency getters, encryption/send authority, public compatibility and accepted writes (#160707, #70401, #163012, #168485, #169405). | | Teams pending-upload dual owners | HOLD: persisting currently memory-only reply consent bytes would change privacy/persistence; deleting SQLite loses restart recovery. Needs an explicit policy choice, not a deslop shortcut. | | Teams streaming, multi-account configuration and exported setup factory | KEEP Stop/partial-delivery/FIFO, credential isolation and published factory signature (#141348, #112811). | | Reef `trust-state-operation.ts:164`, `trust-store.legacy.ts:115` | Share pure seven-command transitions, retain worker/native atomic adapters, schema checks, trust revisions and authorization (#168340). | | Reef `owner-notice.ts:32,72,122,253`, `audit-state.legacy.ts:145–255` | Remove duplicate retry scheduler/in-flight set and synchronous intermediate lease checks; preserve durable recovery/security (#109160, #109380). | | Reef released-host adapter and trust delivery settlement | KEEP declared host compatibility, accepted-write shutdown settlement, peer/key authority and user-data crash recovery. | | X events/allowlist/verification | KEEP paid-event settlement, bounded polling and credential/access authority. | | llama.cpp media/provider/install/orphan owners | KEEP confidentiality of local inputs, digest cache integrity and safe process identity before termination (#167902). | | ClawRouter pool/dashboard | KEEP untrusted network projection, bounded responses and active features; no useful large duplicate justified added abstraction. | | Workboard `view-card-actions.tsx:215`, `view-card.tsx:102`, `view-draft-choices.tsx:6` | Consolidate actions, menu wrappers and card/bulk draft controls; all callers migrated (#168606). | | Workboard native handlers and `view-popover.ts:19` | Drop impossible bound-target guards; repair ordinary conditional-fragment anchor timing (#168606). | | Workboard `sessions-board.ts:149,305`, `change-events.ts:6`, `gateway.ts:211` | Remove duplicate cache/lifecycle fences; share workspace input preparation while retaining workspace/security effect checks. | | Workboard draft/focus/pending-write/editor, board save and label measurement owners | KEEP real unsaved input, async writes, keyboard focus, live-authority checks and measured layout batching. | ## Evidence All local build/test/CLI commands use task-owned HOME, OpenClaw state/config and XDG directories. No real Gateway or user state is used. No timeout increases, retries, skips, new suppressions or weakened retained-behavior baselines. Final proof receipts and exact-head CI attribution are recorded below. Cold compiled-worker preparation dominates several local timings; these are not CI timings or live-provider claims. | Focused local proof | Result / wall cost | | --- | --- | | Codex request diagnostics | 14/14 pass; wrapper445.55s (cold worker/import dominated). | | Codex commands + Doctor contract | 122/123 pass; wrapper1352.60s. Doctor contract passes. The one method-list assertion (`commands.test.ts:951`) also observes background monitor `thread/read` calls. It **reproduces with explicit clean-base source loaded from `56715acf0e5943edecd34fa6f451532cfa9d5f35`**: extra reads followed by the expected `thread/resume`, selected-case8.411s/Vitest403.28s. The affected test/support/actions/bindings/monitor files are byte-unchanged between that base and pinned main. No test skips or timing changes were added;99 unrelated cases were unselected for attribution. | | Workboard backend (sessions-board, Gateway, change-events, registration lifecycle) | 48/48 pass, four files; wrapper587.54s, Vitest545.18s. | | Workboard entire browser scope before final followups; final affected browser suites | 237/237 across29 files in59.03s; final103/103 across6 files in31.95s. New popover regression1/1 in9.34s; unchanged source fails intended geometry assertion in14.57s. | | Workboard actual compiled WebKit consumer | Pass: anchored menu, filter keyboard dismissal, nested Escape preserving dialog, focus return, zero page errors. | | Reef trust/friends/audit/receipt/outbound/notifier | 119/119 across6 files; wrapper927.25s, including cold worker compilation. Earlier unchanged channel proof25/25 pass. | | Teams sqlite/Graph/read authority/setup | 72/72 across5 files; wrapper385.62s. | | Teams Graph contexts/actions | 73/73 across3 files; wrapper327.91s. | | Teams mutation callers/setup policy | 42/42 across5 files; wrapper776.30s. | | Teams resolver + existing channel tests | Resolver4/4 pass; existing channel44 pass/2 fail, wrapper550.01s. **Both failures reproduce on full pinned main `3c63da22f046b15db9d56cf35769f20b398b8c9b`**,44 pass/2 fail, wrapper464.42s: approval-monitor startup timeout120000ms (`channel.test.ts:313`) and subsequent `MSTeams runtime not initialized` (`runtime-store.ts:85` → `monitor.ts:81` → `channel.test.ts:970`). No budgets changed; the second appears cascading, not separately diagnosed. | | Matrix reaction ownership | 11/11 pass; wrapper339.25s. | | Lint suppression contracts | 3/3 pass on frozen candidate; wrapper48.94s. No new suppressions. | | Architecture | Zero runtime value cycles; zero static/Madge components. | Memory owner/sibling proof: 108/109 pass across nine files, wrapper939.49s. The only failure was this patch's newly authored assertion expecting the provider's raw close error instead of the owner's existing normalized diagnostic. After correcting that assertion without a production change, its exact case passed (4.389s execution, Vitest350.74s, wrapper373.90s, dominated by transforms). The other twelve registry cases were unselected in that focused invocation, not skipped in source. Together the runs prove all109 selected contracts, including actual-query retirement, shutdown drain, fallback/reload, healthy probe, transport and deadline behavior. Local tooling notes: the first changed-file run required removing one now-unused assertion-safety allowance. The corrected run passed conflict markers (27.14s), line-cap (4.43s), max-lines (69.87s), and assertion-safety (183.85s), then was intentionally stopped after the full-source SQLite worker inventory produced no result for 681.03s. This was incomplete local proof, not a passing inventory or an inherited source failure. Native production and test extension typegraphs both pass. Scoped lint could not begin analysis because SDK declaration preparation hit its unchanged 300000ms budget, both in the earlier Reef attempt and the final scoped attempt; neither produced a lint diagnostic. Final exact-head hosted CI below closes both gaps, with inventories running on the PR's frozen merge tree. Two custom-config attribution attempts were abandoned for harness setup failures; they are not behavior proof. Teams attribution above uses a normal full-main export and normal harness. No remote lease, live Teams tenant or live provider proof is claimed. Final formatting: all changed source/test/doc files pass. Plugin boundary report passes (zero eligible compatibility removals); UI localization verification passes. No public SDK files/exports or package manifests changed, so an SDK API-surface diff is not applicable. Independent review reported one P2 about an older Workboard read replacing newer `lastKnown` fallback facts before a subsequent backend outage. Declined as the explicitly accepted cache tradeoff, not silently ignored: fallback is presentation-only, availability remains visible, the next successful read repairs it, and `move` independently rereads authoritative facts/scope before its guarded write. The introducing controls are synthetic (#165896/#165141); no user-data, authorization, or persisted-write invariant is relaxed. First hosted CI run `38334064250` on `dabbd9208a20068c24e6901b41a13415c04ac856` completed with two owned lint failures: `check-lint-extensions-2` (explicit boolean and exhaustive return in Reef) and `check-lint-extensions-3` (default generic argument/Promise iterable in Memory, exhaustive return/shadowed local in Workboard). Its `openclaw/ci-gate` failure aggregates those two jobs. All other planned jobs passed, including SQLite inventories, source contracts, types, extension tests, and QA smoke. The focused correction adds five production lines. The first PR-evidence run also failed because this body's headings did not match the required template; corrected headings passed in run `38334357043`. Metadata auto-response cancellations and the superseded evidence run contain no product test suite. No inherited-failure exception is being claimed for these owned failures. **Final exact-head CI passes:** [run 38335564816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38335564816) on `b86c1ba06fa325f178007ba736c294cdd67a566d`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, both extension-lint stripes, full inventories/ratchets, source contracts, typegraphs, selected extension bundles, security, and all QA smoke profiles. This closes the local inventory/lint tooling gaps described above. All exact-head check runs were enumerated; no failed, cancelled, timed-out, or pending check remains. No admin exception, manual rerun, dispatch, or rebase was used. CI job wall seconds: extension bundles 1/2/3/4-1/4-2/5 = 210/160/183/247/137/229; extension lint stripes 2/3 = 145/91; baseline ratchets = 271. These are parallel job wall times including setup, not added test execution time. The lint-only correction also passes native production types, formatting, suppression contracts (3/3; 65.59s wrapper), runtime cycles (0), static/Madge cycles (0), Workboard actions (32/32; 17.93s) and popover (1/1; 16.16s), plus Reef trust/Memory provider lifecycle (51/51; 401.38s Vitest, 445.49s wrapper). Independent review of that delta is scoped-clean at P0–P2; the original explicitly declined display-cache tradeoff remains documented above. ## Visual proof Before/after attachments show the actual built Workboard plugin against synthetic fixture data. Before: details menu at the page origin. After: anchored to its trigger. No pixel-identical claim across fixture timestamps. ![Before: synthetic Workboard details menu at the page origin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4051b726-6af0-45fe-a0b6-e896b1c33a40) ![After: synthetic Workboard details menu anchored to its trigger](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26de3267-537f-46ef-b477-1adb5b0de290)
